title: Shortness of breath — when to get help
content: Call 999 or go to A&E immediately if you have severe difficulty breathing (gasping, choking, or not able to get words out), your chest feels tight or heavy, you have pain that spreads to your arms, back, neck and jaw, your lips or skin are turning very pale, blue or grey, or you feel suddenly confused. Contact NHS 111 if you have difficulty breathing that is more than your usual, you feel or are being sick, you are coughing up blood, you have pain or swelling in one leg, or you have heart palpitations. See a GP if your shortness of breath gets worse with normal activity or when lying down, you have swollen ankles, or you have been coughing for 3 weeks or more.
